name: Saint Lawrence of Brindisi
history: A Capuchin friar of extraordinary gifts: a master of many languages, a tireless preacher, minister general of his order, and a peacemaker trusted by princes. He was chaplain to the imperial army that fought the Turks in Hungary in 1601. John XXIII named him a Doctor of the Church in 1959, the Apostolic Doctor.
life: Giulio Cesare Russo was born at Brindisi in Apulia and was orphaned young. He entered the Capuchins at Verona in 1575 and took the name Lawrence. He studied at Padua and mastered Hebrew, Greek, German, Bohemian and other languages, and knew much of the Bible by heart in its original tongues. Sent to preach in Rome and then across Italy, Austria, Bohemia and Germany, he founded friaries and strengthened Catholics in lands divided by the Reformation. In 1601, as chaplain to the imperial forces at Székesfehérvár in Hungary, he rode before the troops holding a crucifix. Elected minister general in 1602, he visited his friars on foot across Europe. He served as an envoy for peace between Catholic princes, and in 1619 travelled to Lisbon to plead with the king of Spain on behalf of the people of Naples against their viceroy. He died there on his birthday, 22 July.
prayerTo: Saint Lawrence, you used every gift God gave you for the Gospel and for peace. Pray for preachers and scholars, for those who work for peace between nations, and for me, that I may love the Word of God, learn it by heart, and speak up for those who are oppressed. Amen.
penance: Learn one short passage of Scripture by heart today, and do something practical for someone treated unjustly.
meditation: He crossed Europe on foot to plead for the poor of Naples. Whose cause could you take up, even in a small way?
prayer: O God, Who, to enable him to accomplish tasks, no matter how difficult, for the glory of Your name and the salvation of souls, endowed blessed Lawrence, Your Confessor and Doctor, with the spirit of wisdom and fortitude; grant us, in the same spirit, ever to know our duty, and through his prayers to do it. Through our Lord Jesus Christ. Amen.
prayerSource: Collect of the day, Roman Missal of 1962
